rulings.restated: Add w2.one over every confirmed w2 entry, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The line 11 test is 'had more than one employer for 2025', but the program counts W-2 entries. The text does not say whether each W-2 is a distinct employer, so two W-2s from one employer could be miscounted.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The W-2 collection is keyed by employer, and repeated forms from one employer are consolidated into one entry ("Keyed by employer within person; consolidate repeated forms for the same employer explicitly", forms/2025/w2.yaml collection note), so the count of entries is the count of employers that "had more than one employer for 2025" (i1040gi p. 117) asks for. No change to the data.

rulings.restated: Add w2.wages over every confirmed w2 entry, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The IRS text says only 'total wages of more than $176,100' and does not say which W-2 box is meant. The field w2.wages is not defined (box 1 vs. box 3/7), so the operand cannot be confirmed.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The $176,100 test is on social security wages, the wage base above which no social security tax is withheld (i1040gi p. 117, line 11; $10,918.20 is 6.2% of $176,100), so `w2.wages` sums Form W-2 box 3 (social security wages) and box 7 (social security tips), the amounts the tax was withheld on. No change to the data.
